papers.title: Equivariant localizing motives and multiplicative norms on algebraic K-theory
papers.abstract:
We construct multiplicative norms on equivariant nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory for finite groups $G$. We also construct a genuine equivariant version of THH equipped with a Dennis trace map from K-theory compatible with the multiplicative norms. To do so, we follow the general strategy of Blumberg-Gepner-Tabuada in the nonequivariant case by generalizing their category of localizing motives to the genuine equivariant context, building upon the theory of perfect $G$-stable categories of the first-named author. Crucially, we proceed using the recent perspective on noncommutative motives by the second-named author with Sosnilo and Winges which allows us to deal with non-exact functors on this category of motives. Together with an isotropy separation argument for equivariant cubes, we prove our main theorem that norms of stable categories preserve equivariant motivic equivalences. As an immediate consequence, we obtain a unique equivariant multiplicative refinement of nonconnective algebraic $K$-theory.
  From these constructions and results, we draw several applications, namely: (1) that the endofunctor of (equivariant) tensor powers on ordinary perfect stable categories preserve motivic equivalences; (2) that the multiplicative norms also preserve the additive motivic equivalences, thus yielding a motivic refinement of a result of Elmanto-Haugseng and Cnossen-Haugseng-Lenz-Linskens that connective algebraic K-theory admits multiplicative norms; (3) we construct a genuine equivariant version of topological Hochschild homology equipped with a Dennis trace map that is compatible with multiplicative norms; and (4) we prove that every genuine $G$-spectrum is the K-theory of a perfect $G$-stable category.

papers.title: Parametrised functor calculus: excision, spheres, and semiadditivity
papers.abstract: We lay down the foundations of a theory of parametrised functor calculus, generalising parts of the functor calculus of Goodwillie. We introduce the notion of excisable posets and develop a theory of excisive approximations in this context. As an application, we introduce two different excisable posets when parametrising over an atomic orbital category. By comparing the notions of excisiveness for these two posets, we relate the invertibility of certain spheres with Nardin's notion of parametrised semiadditivity, generalising Wirthm\"uller's classical result in equivariant homotopy theory for finite groups.

papers.title: A $\mathbb{C}$-motivic $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1
papers.abstract: Let $\mathrm{DY} = \mathbb{1}/(\eta, \nu) \in \mathrm{SH}(\mathbb{C})$. We construct a $w_1$-self-map of periodicity 1 $w:\Sigma^{5,3}\mathrm{DY} \to \mathrm{DY}.$ The cofiber is a realization of $DA(1)$, the double of the subalgebra $A(1)$ of the $\mathbb{C}$-motivic Steenrod algebra $A$.

papers.title: Involutions on $(\infty,n)$-categories of bordisms and reflection TQFTs
papers.abstract: We construct a strict involution, that is, a strict $\mathbb{Z}/2$-action, on the $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathbf{Bord}_n(H_n)$ of bordisms with $H_n$-structure, where $H_n$ is the symmetry type of a TQFT, using the complete $n$-fold Segal space model. Using this involution, we develop an appropriate definition of reflection TQFTs in this setting and show that they correspond to certain homotopy fixed point spaces. Finally, we apply the machinery to the example of super algebras, where, depending on the symmetry type, the homotopy fixed point data corresponds to either a stellar structure or a real structure on the algebra that the reflection theory assigns to the point.

papers.title: Rational torus equivariant spectra VII: the Cousin complex
papers.abstract:
We explore the analogy between rational G-spectra for an r-torus G and sheaves over an r-dimensional scheme, in the context of the author's algebraic model for rational G-spectra. In particular, the resolution of the sphere of a virtual representation in the standard model corresponds precisely to the Cousin complex resolution of a line bundle.
  The tom Dieck splitting for the sphere of an actual respresentation corresponds to the collapse of the Cousin spectral sequence by degrees, and the the non collapse in other cases corresponds to familiar geometric behaviour.

papers.title: Presentability of categories of localizations and analytic rings
papers.abstract: We prove that certain categories of Bousfield localizations are presentable and give explicit regular cardinals $\kappa$ for which they are $\kappa$-presentable. As an application, we show that the category of analytic rings in the sense of Clausen and Scholze is $(2^{\aleph_0})^+$-presentable.

papers.title: Vector bundles on singular surfaces and threefolds
papers.abstract: We fully classify vector bundles of critical rank on normal affine surfaces and threefolds over algebraically closed fields via their Chern classes. We also prove existence of rank $2$ bundles on threefolds with prescribed first and second motivic Chern classes. The main input is the motivic filtration on algebraic $K$-theory: its third piece is generated by smooth closed points and is identified with motivic cohomology by the third Chern class.

papers.title: A stable multipersistence invariant for ladder modules
papers.abstract: We define an additive functor S that assigns a three parameter persistence module to every morphism between one parameter persistence modules. We show that if the morphism is bar-to-bar, then its image under S is rectangle decomposable. We prove that S is stable with respect to the interleaving distance and study further properties of the functor related to rectangle decompositions.

papers.title: Homology and carrier faces of simplicial distributions
papers.abstract: We study the facial structure of simplicial distribution polytopes using topological and algebraic methods. In the theory of simplicial distributions, measurement and event spaces are represented by simplicial sets, and compatible probability assignments form a convex polytope. Given a simplicial distribution, it is known that its supports determine its carrier face. Moreover, the supports form a simplicial subset of the event space. This naturally raises the question of how the topology of this simplicial subset is related to the corresponding carrier face. Our main objective is to relate the dimension of the carrier face to the topology and combinatorial structure of the space of supports. For $n$-facet-paired measurement spaces, we first express the carrier dimension in terms of the nullity of an associated facet matrix. When the measurement space is additionally orientable, we show that the carrier dimension is determined by the top-dimensional homology of the space of supports, yielding, in particular, a homological criterion for detecting vertices. We then develop an algebraic reduction based on a strong connectivity relation on the generating simplices of the space of supports. This construction yields a reduced facet matrix, indexed by the strongly connected components, whose null space is isomorphic to that of the original facet matrix. As a consequence, both the carrier dimension and extremality can be determined from the topology of the support and the way its strongly connected components are glued together.

papers.title: mixed Hodge structures on the strictly upper triangular Lie algebras
papers.abstract: We show that, for $k\geq 3$, a lattice in the unitriangular Lie group $U_k(\mathbb{R})$ is the fundamental group of a smooth quasi-projective complex algebraic variety if and only if $k=3$. The proof uses the conjugation symmetry and weight conditions of mixed Hodge structure on the Malcev Lie algebra proven by Morgan. This result identifies a family of groups that must be excluded in the search for smooth quasi-projective varieties with torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of high nilpotency class.

papers.title: Operations on $G$-sets and the Dress map
papers.abstract: We study versions of binomial and multichoose coefficients for finite $G$-sets, extending a result of Siebeneicher from the 1970s concerning the duality between these operations. If the group $G$ comes from a finite Galois extension of fields, the Dress map provides a bridge from $G$-sets to quadratic forms over the base field. We show that this Dress map is compatible with binomial coefficients of finite $G$-sets and a particular operation on quadratic forms we define. This allows us to extend the definition of Brugall\'e and Wickelgren's quadratically enriched binomial coefficients to arbitrary Grothendieck--Witt classes. This allows for a new proof that quadratically enriched binomial coefficients depend only on the trace form of the inputted \'etale algebra, as well as an elegant reproof of a result of Chen and Wickelgren about binomial coefficients over finite fields.

papers.title: The Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for p >= 11
papers.abstract: We show that the Smith-Toda complex V(4) exists for all primes p >= 11. This improves on the recently announced result by OpenAI that V(4) exists at the prime 1009.

papers.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
papers.abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.

papers.title: Unitary $S^1$-Manifolds with Four Fixed Points and Kosniowski's Conjecture
papers.abstract: We study unitary \(S^1\)-manifolds with four isolated fixed points in relation to Kosniowski's conjectural inequality \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). For every integer \(m\ge3\), we show that there exists a unitary \(S^1\)-manifold \(M_m^{18}\) with exactly four isolated fixed points, and these manifolds are pairwise distinct and nonzero in ordinary complex bordism. Since \(\chi(M_m^{18})=4\), they give an infinite family of counterexamples to \(4\chi(M)>\dim M\). By gluing two blocks formed by \(G_2/SU(3)\cong S^6\) and the unit disk $D(V)$ of 12- dimensional real $S^1$-representation $V$ along their equivariantly identified free boundaries, we explicitly construct such a manifold $M^{18}_3$. We also prove that the four-point case is null-bordant in real dimension \(16\) and in every real dimension greater than \(18\); hence \(18\) is the smallest dimension in which such a counterexample occurs.

papers.title: $a$-numbers of covers in characteristic two: semigroups and Riemann-Roch spaces
papers.abstract: We compute the $a$-numbers of the Garcia-G\"uneri-Stichtenoth curves, the Beelen-Montanucci curves, and the Skabelund covers of Suzuki curves in characteristic two. The proofs use the identity $a(X)=\ell(\tfrac12\operatorname{div}(dt))$ and reduce the calculations to Riemann-Roch spaces on the base curves. We obtain transfer formulas for odd-degree radical covers, with one or several points at infinity, and evaluate them using Weierstrass semigroups and plane sections of the Hermitian curve. For the first two families we also give cyclic models over the projective line and relate the formulas to Elkin's rank formula. We then treat two classes of Artin-Schreier fibre products. A supersingular genus-six family has a-number $3$ at the zero parameter and $2$ elsewhere, although the genera and $a$-numbers of its quadratic quotients remain fixed. We determine its Ekedahl--Oort types as $(0,0,0,1,2,3)$ and $(0,1,1,2,3,4)$,

papers.title: $R$-trivial Galois cohomology classes and cohomological $p$-dimension
papers.abstract: Given a prime $p$, a field $F$ of characteristic different from $p$ and a finite $p$-primary Galois module $V$, a Galois cohomology class in $H^n(F,V)$ is called $R$-trivial if it can be connected to $0$ by a class defined over an open subscheme of the projective line. All classes of $H^n(F,V)$ are $R$-trivial if $F$ has cohomological $p$-dimension at most $n$, by the Bloch-Kato conjecture. We show that this bound is sharp: working over fields of iterated Laurent series, we produce, for every $n\geq 1$, a field $F$ of cohomological $p$-dimension $n+1$ and a Galois module $V$ such that $H^n(F,V)$ contains classes which are not $R$-trivial. The module $V$ is a quotient of the permutation module on the affine hyperplanes of an elementary abelian $p$-group, arising as a quotient of the absolute Galois group of $F$. We also describe $R$-trivial classes as sums of corestrictions of cup products involving a Kummer class.

papers.title: A Bipartite Graph with a Nonunimodal Acyclic Polynomial
papers.abstract: We construct a bipartite graph on 230 vertices whose acyclic polynomial, which enumerates vertex subsets inducing forests, is not unimodal. This answers Question 3.3 of Barton, Brown, and Pike negatively. The graph has a common set of 50 vertices and 15 branches, each with two sets of six vertices. A partition according to the number of selected common vertices gives a three-term formula for the complete induced-forest polynomial. Its coefficients have a strict descent from degree 62 to degree 63 and a later strict ascent from degree 66 to degree 67. The actual graph, the unrestricted subset-counting formula, and the exact inequalities have been checked in Lean. HAL deposit: hal-05800225v1.

papers.title: A Counterexample to Affine-Subspace Union Stability under Small Deletions
papers.abstract: We construct a family of affine coordinate subspaces of $\mathbb{F}_2^N$ whose union is the entire space, but for which deleting a $1/N$ fraction from each member removes a fraction larger than $N^{-c}$ from the union, for every fixed $c>0$ and arbitrarily large $N$. Each subspace has codimension $\log_2 N$, and the family has at most $2N^2$ members. The construction uses all monochromatic coordinate conditions of size $k$ on $2k$ distinguished coordinates, where $N=2^k$, and deletes their common intersection with the middle Hamming layer. The exact global loss is $\binom{2k}{k}/4^k$. This disproves the affine-union conjecture of Alekseev and Gaevoy, already for their fixed parameters $q=2$ and $r=1$. The all-exponent, arbitrarily-large-dimension counterexample has been formalized and checked in Lean 4. HAL deposit: hal-05800246v1.

papers.title: A cubulation of the associahedron using a torus-equivariant degeneration of the brick variety
papers.abstract: We describe a mixed subdivision of the $(n-1)$-dimensional Loday associahedron into $(n-1)!$ maximal cells which are combinatorial cubes, and we show that the face poset of this subdivision is isomorphic to the face poset of the subdivision of the $1\times 2\times \dotsb \times (n-1)$ box into unit cubes. More generally, we describe mixed subdivisions of generalized associahedra into pieces which are Minkowski sums of Bruhat interval polytopes. Our subdivisions arise from a torus-equivariant embedded (in a product of flag varieties) degeneration of brick varieties into reduced unions of products of Richardson varieties. The subdivision of Loday's associahedron allows us to `embed' the 1-skeleton of the permutahedron in the boundary of the associahedron.

papers.title: A lean formalization of Roy's strong six exponentials theorem
papers.abstract: We formalize in Lean 4 with Mathlib Roy's strong six exponentials theorem: if $x_1,x_2$ are linearly independent over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$ and $y_1,y_2,y_3$ are linearly independent over $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$, then one of the six products $x_iy_j$ lies outside the $\overline{\mathbb{Q}}$-vector space spanned by $1$ and the logarithms of algebraic numbers. The proof closure uses only Lean's three standard axioms. Along the way the development proves Waldschmidt's transcendence theorem on $\mathbb{G}_a^{d_0}\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d_1}$ in the form used by Roy, and Philippon's multiplicity estimate with derivatives on $\mathbb{G}_a^{d_0}\times\mathbb{G}_m^{d_1}$ over every algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, following Roy's account in Waldschmidt's book. We reproduce the public Lean statements, summarize the mathematical route, and record how the artifact is verified. The code is available at https://github.com/telaviv/strong-six-exponentials.

papers.title: A lower bound for two-interval quantum backflow
papers.abstract: An explicit compactly supported positive-momentum state yields a summed backflow greater than 0.06190 over two unit-duration intervals separated by a gap of 3/2, in units where the reduced Planck constant is 1 and the mass is 1/2. An executable numerical certificate encloses its value approximately between 0.0619551065 and 0.0619551266, conditional on stated arithmetic and library assumptions. The state is defined by stored binary-rational coefficients and is re-integrated with enclosed quadrature and rounding errors. This is a trial-state lower bound, not an optimality result. It exceeds a published conjectural numerical range for equal spacing, but does not establish superiority to the true equal-spacing supremum or publication priority.

papers.title: A Nonunimodal Acyclic Polynomial with All Roots in the Left Half-Plane
papers.abstract: Let $A(G,x)$ count vertex subsets of a graph $G$ that induce forests, by their cardinalities. Barton, Brown, and Pike asked whether failure of coefficient unimodality forces $A(G,x)$ to have a root with positive real part. We give a negative answer. The join of $K_{46}$ with three disjoint copies of $P_3$ has a nonunimodal acyclic polynomial of degree nine, yet all its complex roots have strictly negative real part. We derive the polynomial by classifying induced forests and give its exact positive Hurwitz determinants. A Lean formalization verifies the graph-to-polynomial identity and the full counterexample, using an exact rational Lyapunov certificate for strict stability. HAL deposit: hal-05800220v1.

papers.title: A Poincar\'e-Lefschetz Theorem for Cellular Cosheaves and an Application to the Tropical Homology of Orbifold Toric Varieties
papers.abstract: We begin by presenting a version of the Poincar\'e-Lefschetz theorem for certain cellular cosheaves on a particular subdivision of a CW-complex K. To that end we construct a cellular sheaf on K whose cohomology with compact support is isomorphic to the homology of the initial cosheaf. Thereafter we use the first result to generalise the tropical version of the Lefschetz Hyperplane Section Theorem to some singular tropical toric varieties and singular tropical hypersurfaces.

papers.title: A sqrt(17/2) Lower Bound for Depth Reduction in Explainable Planar k-Center Clustering
papers.abstract: We prove that the factor-$2$ lower bound for depth reduction in explainable planar $k$-center clustering is not tight. For every integer $k\ge2$, an explicit set of $4k$ distinct integer points has both ordinary and explainable $k$-center radius one, while every axis-parallel threshold tree with at most $k$ nonempty leaves and depth less than $k-1$ has radius at least $\sqrt{17/2}$. Thus, for every fixed depth multiplier $H$ and every $C<\sqrt{17/2}$, arbitrarily large instances admit no such tree of depth at most $H\lceil\log_2(k+1)\rceil$ and radius at most $C$ times the optimal explainable radius. The point set is a rescaled tail of the ladder of Deng, Gavva, Karthik, Patel, and Srinivasan. The strengthened analysis uses a four-color packing bound and the exact cluster budget to prove rigidity of every sufficiently small-diameter partition, without an explainability assumption. The complete infinite-family theorem and its unbounded-size corollary have been checked in Lean. The existence of a larger universal constant for logarithmic-depth explanations remains unresolved. HAL deposit: hal-05800242v1.

papers.title: A Three-Polynomial Counterexample to the Generalized Effective Hypercube Nullstellensatz
papers.abstract: We give a counterexample to the proposed extension of the effective Hypercube Nullstellensatz from two polynomials to an arbitrary fixed number of polynomials. For every $n\geq1$, we construct three real polynomials in $2n+1$ variables, of degrees $2,2,1$, respectively. Each is nonzero as a function on the Boolean cube, their product vanishes on the cube, and they have no common Boolean zero. Nevertheless, every polynomial certificate $\sum_{i=1}^3 h_i g_i=1$ on the cube satisfies $\deg\overline{h_1g_1}\geq n+1$, where the bar denotes multilinearization. The construction applies a fresh selector variable to the hard pair of Kothari, Kovacs-Deak, Wang, and Yang. Thus its new ingredient is a short transfer of their existing degree obstruction to the product-zero setting. The full unbounded-degree counterexample has been formalized and checked in Lean 4. HAL deposit: hal-05800244v1.

papers.title: A Topological Quantum Field Theory for Representation Varieties of Torus Links
papers.abstract: We construct a Topological Quantum Field Theory (TQFT) that computes the virtual classes of $G$-representation varieties associated with the fundamental group of a torus link complement. Following the framework established by Gonz\'alez-Prieto, Logares and Mu\~noz for $G$-representation varieties of surface groups, we introduce a suitable bordism whose iteration enables a recursive topological evaluation of these virtual classes. Via this TQFT, we explicitly compute the virtual class of these varieties for the groups $G=\mathrm{AGL}_1(\mathbb{C})$ and $G=\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{C})$.

papers.title: Adelic Galois representations are maximal for almost all Drinfeld modules
papers.abstract: Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, let $q$ be an odd prime power, and set $A=\mathbb{F}_q[T]$ and $F=\mathbb{F}_q(T)$. We study the Galois representations associated with rank $r$ Drinfeld modules of the form $\phi_T=T+g_1\tau+\cdots+g_r\tau^r$, where $g_i\in A$ and $g_r\neq 0$. Ordering the coefficient tuples $\vec{g}=(g_1,\ldots,g_r)$ by their maximum degree, we prove that, for a density-one set of tuples, the $\lambda$-adic Galois representation is surjective for every prime $\lambda$ of $A$, and the adelic Galois image contains $\mathrm{SL}_r(\widehat A)$. Moreover, for every tuple in this set, the index of the adelic image equals the index of the corresponding rank-one determinant representation and hence divides $q-1$. These results extend Zywina's theorem in rank $2$ to arbitrary ranks $r\geq 3$. As a further consequence, we establish the existence of rank $r$ Drinfeld modules with surjective adelic Galois representations for every $r\geq 3$, extending previous existence results which were known for prime values of $r$.

papers.title: Ambient Chow Rings of Debarre--Voisin Fourfolds and the Beauville--Voisin Conjecture
papers.abstract: We prove the Beauville--Voisin conjecture for a very general Debarre--Voisin hyperk\"ahler fourfold \(Y\subset\Gr(6,10)\) associated with a trivector \(\sigma\) on a ten-dimensional complex vector space \(V_{10}\). Namely, the cycle class map is injective on the subalgebra of the Chow ring generated by divisor classes and the Chern classes of the tangent bundle.

papers.title: An Algebraic Abstraction of the Localic Sheafification via the Tripos-to-Topos Construction
papers.abstract: Localic and realizability toposes are two central classes of toposes in categorical logic, both arising from the Hyland, Johnstone and Pitts tripos-to-topos construction. We investigate the common geometric structure underlying these classes by developing an algebraic abstraction of localic presheaves, localic sheafification, and the role of supercompactification in the Comparison Lemma. The resulting framework applies to a broad class of toposes arising from the tripos-to-topos construction, including all $\set$-based triposes. These results establish a common geometric framework encompassing both localic and realizability toposes.

papers.title: An Approximate Solution to the Minimum Vertex Cover Problem: The Salvador Algorithm
papers.abstract: Minimum Vertex Cover has a classical linear-time ratio of $2$, and under the Unique Games Conjecture no polynomial-time algorithm achieves a fixed ratio below $2$ unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$. We present version 0.1.4 of \textsc{Salvador}, a linear-time ensemble of seventeen strategies, numbered in the order in which they are computed: twelve base strategies (component amplification before a maximal matching, the maximal matching itself, degree and weight heuristics, reductions to auxiliary problems that are solved exactly, a decomposition into bipartite layers, a weighted subdivision reduction and a bounded-treewidth dynamic program), followed by five improvers (a union pass, local search, reduce-and-search, consensus forcing and a swap-maximize refinement). We prove that every strategy runs in $O((n+m)\,\alpha(n))$ time, and that the returned cover has at most $2\tau-r$ vertices, where $r$ is the number of components with an edge, so the ratio is at most $1.999999999$ whenever $\tau\le10^{9}r$. We prove exactness or a bounded ratio on several classes of graphs, among them every bipartite graph on which the Hopcroft--Karp phases of the layer strategy reach a maximum matching, and we give a per-instance certificate: a cover with at most $2L-|M|$ vertices, for a lower bound $L\le\tau$ and the maximal matching $M$, is within ratio $3/2$ on that instance. In a reproducible suite the returned cover satisfies $|C|\le2\tau-|M|$ on all $291$ tested graphs with a known optimum and is certified on the six without one, although single strategies violate it; on the $68$ DIMACS clique complements it is never worse than Hvala and optimal on $37$ instances against $18$. Whether $|C|\le2\tau-|M|$ holds on every graph is stated as a conjecture: a proof would give a linear-time $3/2$-approximation and would refute the Unique Games Conjecture unless $\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}$.

papers.title: An Euler-product mollifier for the Jensen moment of zeta and an energy criterion for the Riemann hypothesis
papers.abstract: The Jensen moment of Balazard, Saias and Yor expresses the zeros of the Riemann zeta function outside the critical line through the mean value of the logarithm of its absolute value on that line. Jensen's inequality converts any mollifier into an upper bound for this contribution. For Dirichlet-polynomial mollifiers, the bound cannot fall below 0.0386, a barrier arising from the pole at s = 1. We instead use the reciprocal of a smoothed Euler factor, denoted E-star(X,s), constructed from prime powers up to a constant multiple of X together with an explicit pole term. The quotient of the zeta function by this factor is then expressed solely in terms of its nontrivial zeros. We prove that the resulting bound B(X,s0), for any center s0 with real part greater than one half, tends to zero under the Riemann hypothesis (RH). Consequently, RH is equivalent to the convergence of B(X,s0) to zero. If the supremum of the real parts of the zeros is attained and exceeds one half, the bound grows at least as fast as X to a positive power divided by log X. Under the same attainment assumption, RH is therefore equivalent to boundedness, as X tends to infinity, of a single weighted mean-square energy: the integral over the real line of the squared absolute value of zeta divided by E-star on the critical line, weighted by 1/(1+t squared). Numerically, the bound decreases to 0.0015 at X = 10,000 for the Balazard–Saias–Yor center s0 = 1. At s0 = 2, it decreases approximately as 0.037 divided by log X up to X = 1,000,000, close to a heuristic prediction involving the constant kappa = 1.828... . By contrast, the corresponding quantity grows for the Davenport–Heilbronn function. We describe the geometry of the factorization and use two control functions to identify the additional ingredients required for a proof of boundedness of the mean-square energy.

papers.title: Approximation and extension theorems for normal affine toric varieties
papers.abstract: We study approximation and extension problems for holomorphic maps from Stein spaces to normal affine toric varieties, continuing the work of L\"ark\"ang and L\'arusson. Normality allows us to obtain twisted factorizations for arbitrary holomorphic maps from factorial complex spaces, including degenerate maps. This yields approximation and extension theorems under weaker cohomological assumptions. We also prove a simultaneous approximation and extension theorem under an additional codimension condition on the inverse image of the singular locus and a cohomological condition on the union of the interpolation submanifold and the approximation set. Finally, an explicit example with target $\{w^2=uv\}\cong\mathbb{C}^2/\{\pm1\}$ shows that simultaneous approximation and extension can fail even when the relevant cohomological obstructions vanish. Thus normality alone does not recover the full approximation and interpolation property of Oka manifolds.

papers.title: Arithmetic structure in a complete atlas of power-residue runs below $2^{32}$: Rabung profiles, Kummer densities, norm dependencies, and local codes
papers.abstract: We study the arithmetic behind long runs in a complete census of power-residue colourings below $2^{32}$, covering every admissible order $2\le r\le9$. The dataset contains $203\,280\,221$ primes and $677\,591\,249$ profiles, with exact quadratic four-window counts at every odd prime. A bounded study of its deep tail identifies algebraic windows with fewer independent character conditions than their lengths suggest. We certify their power-class groups and conjugate-root overlaps, obtaining exact Kummer densities for fixed templates, including eight additional order-four models. In a quadratic family, eleven constant positions force twenty-six neutral positions at odd character orders. In two further families, norm identities generate all remaining higher-root relations. A length-$53$ cubic realizes a three-wise independent binary code whose monochromatic probability is $4096$ times that of independent signs; its local run law is computed exactly. A separate stratified million-profile ternary sample is analysed with the same finite catalogue filter applied to the data and to an independent-colour comparator. Finite census statements, selected explanations and asymptotic template laws concern distinct populations. No universal law of global maxima or finite-range error estimate for the template densities is asserted.

papers.title: Bousfield--Kan Completions of Subcontractible Presentations
papers.abstract: We study Bousfield--Kan completions through the interaction of free simplicial resolutions, their filtration spectral sequences, and a noncommutative arithmetic square. For every free discrete simplicial group of finite type, we express its integral pronilpotent completion as the homotopy pullback of its rational prounipotent completion and the product of its pro-$p$ completions over an explicit adelic simplicial group. The adelic entry is formed by taking restricted products at finite nilpotent stages and then their inverse limit; no nilpotency assumption on the original group of components is required. Finite subpresentations of contractible presentations provide an explicit application of this construction. Independence of the specified relators makes the positive-degree terms of the rational and mod-$p$ filtration spectral sequences vanish, with convergence verified on the quotient towers. Continuous comparison of free simplicial resolutions then realizes, in characteristic zero, the equivalence with a constant free prounipotent group by morphisms and homotopies in that category. For the corresponding presentation complex $K$ we obtain $R_\infty K\simeq K(F_R(Z),1)$ for $R=\mathbb Q,\mathbb F_p,\mathbb Z$, where $Z$ indexes a complementary basis and $F_R(Z)$ denotes, respectively, the rational points of a free prounipotent group, a free pro-$p$ group, or a free pronilpotent group. Compatible contractions at the nilpotent stages identify all four entries of the arithmetic square in this case.

papers.title: Brauer-Manin obstruction for symmetric powers
papers.abstract: For a quasi-projective smooth geometrically integral variety $X$ over a number field, we prove that the Brauer-Manin obstruction for its symmetric powers coincides with the obstruction coming from $X$. As a consequence, Brauer-Manin obstruction for the symmetric powers cannot provide new cohomological obstruction to weak approximation of zero-cycles for $X$. The key intermediate ingredients are a Dold-Thom type result for Brauer groups and a precise descent formula for adelic points.

papers.title: Class field theory for function fields and finite abelian torsors
papers.abstract: Let $U$ be a smooth and connected curve over an algebraically closed field of positive characteristic, with smooth compactification $X$. We generalize classical Geometric Class Field theory to provide a classification of fppf $G$-torsors over $U$ in terms of isogenies of generalized Jacobians, for any finite abelian group scheme $G$. We then apply this classification to give a novel description of the abelianized Nori fundamental group scheme of $U$ in terms of the Serre--Oort fundamental groups of generalized Jacobians of $X$; when $U=X$ is projective, we recover a well known description of the abelianized fundamental group scheme of $X$ as the projective limit of all torsion subgroup schemes of its Jacobian.

papers.title: Classification of real Lie algebras of dimension one, two and three
papers.abstract:
We present an exhaustive, self-contained, and coordinate-free structural classification of real Lie algebras of dimensions one, two, and three up to isomorphism. In dimensions one and two, the classification is governed entirely by the derived ideal and elementary derivation theory. In dimension three, we develop the classical exterior duality isomorphism $\Lambda^2\mathfrak{g} \cong \mathfrak{g}^* \otimes \Lambda^3\mathfrak{g}$ pioneered by Bryant and Milnor, which reduces the quadratic Jacobi identity on the $3 \times 3$ structure matrix $C = S + \hat{a}$ to the linear orthogonality relation $S \cdot a = 0$, where $a = \frac{1}{2}\chi$ is the trace covector.
  We systematically bifurcate the three-dimensional category into unimodular ($a = 0$) and non-unimodular ($a \neq 0$) sectors, completely recovering the nine classical Bianchi isomorphism classes (Bianchi types I through IX) alongside their continuous moduli invariants. Furthermore, we establish the Levi--Malcev decomposition for low dimensions, compute the exact minimal representation dimension $\mu(\mathfrak{g})$ via Ado's Theorem by constructing explicit matrix realizations in $\mathfrak{gl}(\mu, \mathbb{R})$, and formulate a deterministic, coordinate-free decision algorithm for algebra identification.

papers.title: Computing S(X) for Ruled Surfaces Defined by Stable Bundles on Curves of Genus 2
papers.abstract: This paper discusses the algebra of symmetric tensors for ruled surfaces defined by rank 2 stable vector bundles on curves of genus 2. The algebra is computed for special bundles $E$ when $S^2 E$ is destabilized by a line bundle and when $S^3 E$ is destabilized by a bundle of rank 2. A strategy for computation is discussed in regards to the other special bundles $E$. This paper also discusses the generalization of these strategies to higher genus and gives a computation when $E$ is not stable and may be written as a direct sum of line bundles.

papers.title: Continuous Comparison of Free Simplicial Prounipotent and Pro-$p$ Resolutions
papers.abstract: We give a continuous version of the comparison theorem for free simplicial resolutions in the categories of prounipotent groups over a field of characteristic zero and of pro-$p$ groups. The resolutions carry free bases compatible with degeneracies; their ranks may be infinite. In characteristic zero the lifting step follows from continuous linear splittings and the universal property of completed free Lie algebras. In the pro-$p$ case it follows from the classical projectivity of free pro-$p$ groups. A relative lifting argument and an explicit simplicial cylinder establish homotopy uniqueness. We formulate the free bases using actual surjections in the simplex category, so degeneracy words related by simplicial identities are identified from the outset, and we spell out the full matching objects used in the lifting argument. The question arose naturally in our preceding work on Bousfield--Kan completions of subcontractible presentations.

papers.title: Counterexamples to the multicolor nonnested matching conjecture
papers.abstract: We show that excluding nested pairs can increase the number of vertices needed to force a matching of one color, disproving a conjecture of Barát, Gyárfás and Tóth. A matching consists of edges with no shared endpoint. In a fixed vertex order, two edges are nested if both endpoints of one lie between those of the other. For $r$ colors and a target of $k$ edges, the classical theorem guarantees a matching of one color on $(r-1)(k-1)+2k$ vertices when every pair is joined by an edge. For every $r,k\ge3$, we construct a coloring at this very threshold in which every such matching contains a nested pair. Thus the nonnested threshold is larger by at least one vertex. Already with three colors, ten vertices force three disjoint edges of one color, while our coloring makes every such triple contain a nested pair. The self-contained proof combines endpoint counts with two edge recolorings that obstruct the pairings allowed by the vertex order.

papers.title: Counting symmetric unimodular triangulations
papers.abstract: The objects of study are triangulations of the dilated standard triangle in the plane. Motivated by work on T-curves (Geiselmann et al., 2026), the focus lies on unimodular triangulations with a fixed symmetry axis. Lower and upper bounds are given, in combination with full enumerations of a few small cases.

papers.title: Cubic-residue quadruplets: elliptic formulas and arithmetic fluctuations
papers.abstract: Let $A_p$ count the monochromatic consecutive four-windows of a nontrivial cubic character modulo a prime $p\equiv1\pmod3$, with zero excluded and overlapping windows counted separately. We give an exact formula for $A_p$ in terms of fixed elliptic traces and a finite boundary correction. Its complex-multiplication terms are related cubic twists. This produces two arithmetic fluctuation regimes: the first four moments of $(27A_p-p)/\sqrt p$ tend to $(0,44,0,4224)$ when three is a cube and to $(0,17,0,738)$ otherwise. Over all admissible primes they tend to $(0,26,0,1900)$. The proof combines a four-position identity following from Greene's hypergeometric formalism and Lennon's trace formula with symmetric-power automorphy, cyclic base change and a finite collection of Rankin-Selberg prime number theorems; it uses no GRH. A direct geometric proof exposes the phases and exceptional points, with the genus-two and isogeny constructions of Freeman-Satoh and Guillevic-Vergnaud explicitly credited. Point-order and Hasse certificates verify numerical examples without enumerating their billion-position character words. The conclusions concern fixed pattern length and four moments; no complete limiting distribution, constant-order centring of the raw count, or law for logarithmic-length maxima is proved.

papers.title: Cuspidal distinction via intertwining periods
papers.abstract: Local intertwining periods have so far been used to reduce distinction of a general irreducible representation to distinction of cuspidal ones, for which other tools -- type theory, local and global trace formulae -- take over. The main contribution of this paper is to prove that they can be used to decide distinction of cuspidal representations themselves. We develop this approach with three well-studied examples for which the ambient group is an inner form of $\mathrm{GL}_n$ over a $p$-adic field, namely linear models, their non-split twisted version, and the quaternionic symplectic model. As consequences, we obtain proofs valid in arbitrary residual characteristic of the cuspidal case of the epsilon dichotomy conjecture of Prasad and Takloo-Bighash and of Prasad's conjecture on quaternionic symplectic models. The proof in the quaternionic symplectic model case, although going through intertwining periods, uses the simplest ones, namely closed intertwining periods, and is disappointingly short and elementary.

papers.title: Decorated trees
papers.abstract: We study a class of combinatorial objects that we call "decorated trees". These consist of vertices, arrows and edges, where each edge is decorated by two integers (one near each of its endpoints), each arrow is decorated by an integer, and the decorations are required to satisfy certain conditions. The class of decorated trees includes different types of trees used in algebraic geometry, such as the Eisenbud and Neumann diagrams for links of singularities and the Neumann diagrams for links at infinity of algebraic plane curves. By purely combinatorial means, we recover some formulas that were previously understood to be "topological". In this way, we extend the generality of those formulas and show that they are in fact "combinatorial".

papers.title: Deligne--Faltings Logarithmic Derived Geometry with a View towards Logarithmic GLSM
papers.abstract: Many perfect obstruction theories and virtual cycles in enumerative geometry are shadows from derived geometry. In this paper, we give a general construction of reduced perfect obstruction theories arising from a geometric reduction of the derived stack $X$ with respect to a $(-1)$-shifted log function $w_\alpha$. Notably, this construction leads to a decomposition of the virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{vir}}$ into the reduced virtual cycle $[X]^{\mathrm{red}}$ and a reduced boundary cycle $[\Delta_X]^\red$. Our construction is motivated by future applications to the moduli stack of UMD logarithmic R-maps in log GLSM \cite{CJR21}. Along the way, we develop logarithmic analogs of several constructions in derived geometry, in particular proving a logarithmic Lagrangian intersection theorem.

papers.title: Dg models for derived differential operators
papers.abstract: We show that for any algebra $R$ that is essentially of finite type over a field $k$, the derived functors of Smith-Van den Bergh admit a dg enhancement. In particular, for any $R$-module $M$ one can associate a dg algebra of differential operators $E_M$ whose cohomology is a nilpotent thickening of the (classical) ring of $k$-linear differential operators on $M$. We show that these dg algebras fit into a framework of Koszul duality due to Dwyer-Greenlees and specializes to a derived ring of differential operators studied by Yang when $M=R$ and $k=\mathbb{C}$. In particular, upon fixing a presentation $R=S/I$ with $S$ essentially smooth, we show a derived Kashiwara's equivalence, namely that whenever $\mathrm{supp}_S(M)=\mathrm{V}(I)$ then there is an equivalence of triangulated categories between the derived category of dg ${E}_M$-modules and the derived category of $D$-modules on $S$ that are set-theoretically supported on $I$. Finally, in the case of positive characteristic, we show that the dg algebra ${E}_M$ admits a description in terms of the Frobenius endomorphism akin to the classical description of differential operators, and the proof employs simplicial techniques to obtain a result of independent interest in commutative algebra.

papers.title: Equivalued affine springer fibers in mixed characteristic
papers.abstract: We study Witt-vector affine Springer fibers for tame equi-valued conjugacy classes in tamely ramified groups. Following the approach of Goresky-Kottwitz-MacPherson in the equal characteristic setting, we show that they admit pavings by iterations of perfections of affine space bundles whose base are smooth Hessenberg varieties. Along the way we revisit a version of the Chevalley restriction theorem for the dual of Lie algebras.

papers.title: Equivariant Chow functions and Wonderful Models in type A and B
papers.abstract: We prove a general inversion formula in the equivariant incidence algebras of geometric lattices that relates the equivariant Chow function with the equivariant super-reduced characteristic function. We apply this result to the case of minimal wonderful models for hyperplane arrangements associated to root systems, with the natural action of the corresponding Weyl group. Applying this formula to type $A$ (i.e. the partition lattices), we recover Getzler's compositional identity in type $A$. In type $B$ (i.e. the signed partition lattice), we recover Henderson's result, expressing the equivariant Chow generating series in terms of the same series in type $A$ and the equivariant characteristic generating series of type $B$. Moreover, we obtain a new compositional identity for the equivariant Chow generating series.

papers.title: Euclidean Distance Optimization Within the Grassmannian
papers.abstract: Given a subvariety of the Grassmannian and a data point, we seek to find a point on the subvariety minimizing the Euclidean distance to the data point. The number of complex critical points of this optimization problem is the Euclidean distance (ED) degree. We show that the ED discriminant of the whole Grassmannian, that is, the set of data points with a number of critical points different than the ED degree, is the discriminant of the characteristic polynomial of the data as a projection matrix. Another closely connected algebraic complexity measure for a subvariety in the Grassmannian is the Grassmann distance (GD) degree, which is the number of complex critical points of the distance optimization problem when the data point itself is in the Grassmannian. We give formulae for ED and GD degrees of geometrically meaningful subvarieties of the Grassmannian, namely, products of smaller Grassmannians, matroid realization varieties, and Schubert varieties.

papers.title: Extra-fine sheaves and interaction decompositions
papers.abstract: We introduce an original notion of (upper) extra-fine sheaf on a topological space, for which \v{C}ech cohomology in strictly positive degree vanishes. We apply this notion when the topological space is a partially ordered set (poset) equipped with the Alexandroff topology and the sheaves are made of duals of decomposable functors of vector spaces. The decomposition of the functor is known as interaction decomposition and can be expressed by a novel sum-intersection condition. We use these results to compute the dimension of the space of global sections when the sheaves are derived from those freely generated over a presheaf (of finite sets); this generalizes and makes topological classical counting formulae for the number of solutions of the linearized marginal problem (Kellerer and Mat\'u\v{s}). We finish with a comparison theorem between the \v{C}ech cohomology associated to a covering and the topos cohomology of the poset with coefficients in the presheaf, which is also the cohomology of a cosimplicial local system over the nerve of the poset. For that, we give a detailed treatment of cosimplicial local systems on simplicial sets. The appendixes present presheaves, sheaves relative \v{C}ech cohomology, and their application to the marginal problem.

papers.title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
papers.abstract: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,\sigma,\chi_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.

papers.title: Folding to the Bessel-Clifford system, and Equivariant Topological Recursion
papers.abstract: We study the interplay between symmetry reductions of meromorphic connections, folding, and topological recursion. As a motivating example, we realize the Bessel-Clifford system as a folding of a symmetry-invariant subspace of the $0-$member of the Painlev\'e IV hierarchy. We introduce equivariant topological recursion for spectral curves with a Klein four-group $\mathbb Z_2\times\mathbb Z_2$ symmetry and prove that the corresponding equivariant correlators can be folded to the ordinary topological recursion correlators on the quotient spectral curve. We further establish the compatibility of this folding with the associated wave functions and quantum curves. In the Bessel-Clifford example, this yields an explicit relation between the equivariant and folded wave functions and recovers the corresponding quantum curve reduction. These results provide a framework for relating symmetry reductions of integrable systems to folding operations in topological recursion.

papers.title: Gaussian weights on fractals and Edelman's ghosts and shadows
papers.abstract: Can a Gaussian on a noninteger-dimensional fractal give a probabilistic realization of Edelman's ghosts and shadows? We distinguish a Gaussian-weighted Hausdorff measure, a radial Gaussian law, and a Gaussian random vector or field. For every real $\beta>1$, we construct a closed cone of Hausdorff dimension $\beta$ whose Gaussian-weighted $\beta$-dimensional Hausdorff measure has exactly the $\chi_\beta$ radial distribution. The construction relies on exact radial volume growth, not merely on a dimension calculation. We prove a metric obstruction below dimension one and explain why the cone does not supply ordinary Gaussian addition or a scalar algebra. A separate Gram-determinant argument rules out preserving all polynomially continued Euclidean Gaussian Gram identities in a positive model. We then give proofs of the angular beta-gamma identities, associativity of Bessel-Kingman convolution, and its Gaussian convolution semigroup for $\beta\geq1$. Squared Bessel processes, tridiagonal and bidiagonal matrix models, Dunkl Gaussians, and Gaussian fields on fractals provide complementary constructions with explicitly different meanings of dimension. None of these statements asserts the existence of a full noninteger-dimensional scalar algebra.

papers.title: Generic vanishing for Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties
papers.abstract: We study generic vanishing for the Dolbeault cohomology of mixed Hodge modules, where the differentials in the Dolbeault complex are modified by a one-form. We prove that, on the Dolbeault moduli space of Higgs line bundles, the cohomology support loci of mixed Hodge modules agree with the images of the cohomology support loci of their underlying $\mathscr{D}$-modules on the de Rham moduli space under the map induced by the nonabelian Hodge correspondence. We further apply this result to study Fourier-Mukai transforms of mixed Hodge modules on abelian varieties. We show that the extended Fourier-Mukai transform for bounded complexes of mixed Hodge modules has cohomology sheaves that are flat over the twistor line of $\lambda$-connections. This also gives an extension of Fourier transform of mixed Hodge modules to a compactification of the de Rham moduli space.

papers.title: Geometric characterization of $p$-exceptional monomial GAPN functions
papers.abstract:
On finite fields of characteristic $p$, PN (perfect nonlinear) functions for odd $p$ and APN (almost perfect nonlinear) functions for even $p$ are well-known classes of highly nonlinear functions. GAPN (generalized almost perfect nonlinear) functions were introduced as a generalization of APN functions for even $p$ to all $p$. One of the main targets of studies on such highly nonlinear functions is their classification. While $p$-exceptional monomial PN and $2$-exceptional monomial APN functions have been classified, the corresponding problem for GAPN functions remains open. Here, a polynomial over $\mathbb{F}_p$ is called a $p$-exceptional PN (resp. APN, resp. GAPN) function if it is a PN (resp. APN, resp. GAPN) function on $\mathbb{F}_{p^n}$ for infinitely many positive integers $n$.
  In this paper, we give a geometric characterization of $p$-exceptional monomial GAPN functions. To this end, for a prime power $q$, we establish a geometric characterization of non-zero polynomials in $\mathbb{F}_{q}[x,y]$ having no absolutely irreducible factor defined over $\mathbb{F}_{q}$.

papers.title: Ghosts in Poisson Brane Gases
papers.abstract:
A Poisson gas of branes with mass intensity $
u$ dresses the graviton propagator by the random entire function $\prod_k(1+p^2/t_k)$. We prove that the gas average of the propagator equals $p^{-2}\exp[-\int p^2
u(\dd t)/(p^2+t)]$, so that the massive states carry total weight $e^{-
u(0,\infty)}-1<0$. For $
u=\lambda(t)\,\dd t/t$ the averaged spectrum consists of ghosts alone exactly when $\lambda\le1$, and every average with a finite four-dimensional tadpole has states of both signs. Frozen gases keep alternating residues.

papers.title: Hyperbolicity and fundamental groups of complex quasi-projective varieties (III): applications
papers.abstract: This paper is Part III of a series of three. We begin by introducing the notion of $h$-special varieties, which can be seen as varieties "chain-connected by the Zariski closures of entire curves." We prove that if $X$ is either a special smooth complex quasi-projective variety in the sense of Campana or an $h$-special variety, then for any linear representation $\rho:\pi_1(X)\to {\rm GL}_N(\mathbb{C})$, the image $\rho(\pi_1(X))$ is virtually nilpotent. We also provide examples showing that this result is sharp, leading to a revised form of Campana's abelianity conjecture for smooth quasi-projective varieties. In addition, we prove a structure theorem for quasi-projective varieties with big and semisimple representations of the fundamental groups, thereby addressing a conjecture by Koll\'ar in 1995. We also construct several examples of quasi-projective varieties that are special and $h$-special, highlighting certain atypical properties of the non-compact case in contrast with the projective setting.

papers.title: Hypercube Richardson varieties from magic words
papers.abstract: Inspired by the recent preprint of Ellenberg, Libedinsky, Plaza, Simental, and Williamson, we study the geometry of Richardson varieties whose associated Bruhat intervals are boolean posets. We define magic words for a Bruhat interval and prove that for intervals with magic words the associated Richardson variety is a tower of $\mathbb{P}^1$-s. We also prove that the Bruhat intervals consisting of the dyadically well-distributed permutations all have magic words. This gives a new proof that they form a boolean poset.

papers.title: Identifiability from Moments in Independent Component Analysis Mixture Models
papers.abstract: We study Independent Component Analysis (ICA) mixture models. These models consist of mixtures of ICA densities. An ICA density is associated with a random vector whose coordinates become mutually independent after an invertible linear transformation. ICA mixture models are nonparametric extensions of the celebrated family of Gaussian mixtures. We show that in many cases the ICA mixtures are identifiable from the collection of the observed moment tensors, that is, the mixing coefficients, linear transformations, and source moments of order up to $d$ can be identified from the moment tensors of order up to $d$ for generic parameters. We address the problem by studying the corresponding secant varieties and their algebraic properties such as dimensions and Gauss maps. In particular, for $n$-variate distributions, we establish that generically and up to the trivial scaling and permutation symmetries, when $d\geq 5$, the parameters can be recovered uniquely for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ mixture components. For $d=3,4$, we show identifiability up to a finite equivalence class for asymptotically up to $n^{d-2}/d!$ and $0.5 n^{d-2}/d!$ components respectively, where for $d=4$ the mixing coefficients need to be known a priori. The obtained bounds on the component numbers have the maximum possible orders in $n$, and for $d = 3$ and $d\geq 5$, they are also asymptotically sharp.

papers.title: Integral root fibers and closed factorizations: Pairing maps, Rees covariance, caps, and sewing
papers.abstract: We construct rootwise and formal Rees boundary data from the marked modules and lattices of the companion boundary-module construction, keeping their distinct coefficient and completion domains. Using a Newton interpolation basis, we determine the Smith invariants and the integral image of the map induced by the Hopf pairing. Factorial/Rees covariance and compatible finite-stage representatives produce a strict rootwise/Rees module with its theta endpoint. At an admissible odd prime, no continuous homomorphism extends algebraic root specialization to the entire completed Rees source; further obstructions exclude unrestricted Newton padding and a state-natural lift of a contracted scalar identity. Established perturbative, Habiro, and stated-skein/Morita constructions give closed comparisons after the declared cap or sewing map, with their boundary state objects kept separate.

papers.title: Lefschetz Pencils on surfaces and an application to Seshadri constants
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a nonsingular complex projective surface and let $L$ be a very ample line bundle on $X$. We study the question: when does a general pencil in the linear system $|L|$ consist of only irreducible and reduced curves? We give a precise condition which guarantees an affirmative answer: in fact, this holds if and only if the genus of a general member of $|L|$ exceeds the irregularity of $X$. The proof is topological, using vanishing cycles and the theory of Lefschetz pencils. As an application, combined with a construction due to Miranda, we prove that for any positive rational number $\delta$ there exist a blow up $Y \to X$ at finitely many points, an ample line bundle $M$ on $Y$ and a point $x \in Y$ such that $\varepsilon(Y,M,x) = \delta$; Miranda proved this when $X = \mathbb{P}^2$.

papers.title: Local topological zeta functions of generic symmetric and catalecticant determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: We give explicit formulas for the local topological zeta functions at the origin of generic symmetric determinantal varieties and catalecticant determinantal varieties associated with generic Hankel matrices. In the symmetric determinant hypersurface case, the formula simplifies to a closed product expression and implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture. For catalecticant determinantal varieties, we establish a simultaneous local reduction of the determinantal ideals and obtain a closed product formula for their local topological zeta functions. Together with the known Bernstein-Sato polynomial of the Hankel determinant, this also implies the Strong Monodromy Conjecture in the square catalecticant determinant case. The method used in this paper also gives short proofs of Chen-Zuo/Docamposs formula in the generic determinantal case and Chen-Shi-Xu-Zuo's formula in the skew-symmetric case.

papers.title: Locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras
papers.abstract: For an Artin algebra $\Lambda$, we define the class of locally Gorenstein modules, which is a generalization of semi-Gorenstein projective modules and, therefore, a generalization of projective Gorenstein modules. For a locally Gorenstein module $X\in{\rm mod}\ \Lambda$ we construct $\underline{{\chi}}_X$ a subcategory of $\underline{{\rm mod}}$ $\Lambda$ and we prove that the syzygy functor is faithful and full on $\underline{{\chi}}_X$. Using that, we prove that the Igusa-Todorov functions $\phi$ and $\psi$ vanish on the family of locally Gorenstein modules. Finally, using locally Gorenstein modules, we define the locally Gorenstein algebras, a generalization of Gorenstein algebras, and we prove that their finitistic, and the $\phi$ and $\psi$ dimensions are finite.

papers.title: Logarithmic Crystalline Representations
papers.abstract: In 1989, Faltings proved the comparison theorem between \'etale cohomology and crystalline cohomology by studying Fontaine-Faltings modules and crystalline representations. In his paper, he mentioned these modules and representations can be extended to the logarithmic context, but without detail. This note aims to explicitly present the construction of logarithmic Fontaine-Faltings modules and logarithmic crystalline representations.

papers.title: Low-weight compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ and the extended Torelli morphism
papers.abstract: We study the weight zero and weight two graded pieces of the compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal M_{g,n}^{ct}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus $g$ of compact type and show that they are computed by bridgeless graph complexes. In weight two, we construct a natural embedding of shifted weight zero cohomology from lower genus. For unmarked curves, we construct canonical classes represented by pinched odd wheel graphs and prove that distinct wheel monomials give linearly independent classes in the dual of $W_0H_c^{2g}(\mathcal M_g^{ct};\mathbb Q)$. By relating the bridgeless graph complex to the $K$-theory of graphs and the Quillen spectral sequence, we show that these classes remain linearly independent after pushforward along the extended Torelli morphism $\mathcal M_g^{ct}\to\mathcal A_g$. Finally, we prove that the realizations of the motivic Lie algebra arising from $\mathcal M_g$ and $\mathcal A_g$ have the same image in the weight zero compactly supported cohomology of $\mathcal M_g^{ct}$.

papers.title: Marked Heegaard Boundary Modules: Filling, Joint Completion, and Integral Lattices
papers.abstract: A marked handlebody state must retain its filling relations and coefficient control before complementary capping or root specialization. We construct boundary modules and regulated integral lattices that keep the disk and cyclotomic residues of one finite-stage representative together. Standard handle-attachment and recoupling results supply the geometric inputs; the comparison constructs endpoint lattices, separating transport, raw and saturated quotient towers, and exact cap domains. These objects supply the companion rootwise theory, while the two completed topologies remain distinct and root specialization remains restricted to its declared domain.

papers.title: Mass Gap of Lattice Yang--Mills Theory up to the Dobrushin Ceiling
papers.abstract: We prove that the Hessian of the Wilson action on $d$-dimensional lattice gauge fields is bounded by $4d$, sharply, so lattice $\SU(N)$ Yang--Mills theory has a unique infinite-volume state with a positive mass gap for $|\beta|<1/(8d)$. Every von Mises--Fisher law on the three-sphere moves by at most a quarter of its parameter in Kantorovich distance; consequently four-dimensional $\SU(2)$ theory has a mass gap for $\beta_W<2/9$, the ceiling of all single-link Dobrushin arguments. A gauge-invariant finite-box criterion for decay and the area law is also given. The continuum mass gap remains open.

papers.title: Moving prime environments and arithmetic cluster limits
papers.abstract: We study shrinking-target occurrences of completely multiplicative functions with arbitrarily moving phases on a fixed finite set of exceptional primes and independent Haar values at the remaining primes. After exact removal of the environment-only points, effective integer-subgroup profiles classify all subsequential marked cluster limits, while target-scale pair overlaps characterize Poisson convergence. The quantitative input is a direct Haar comparison with the moving germ kernel, uniform in the exceptional phases and with stretched-exponential error. For deterministic profiles and interval targets, the complete spatial covariance measure reconstructs the unmarked law through primitive multiplicative rays and finite interval geometry. A positive forest formula makes this reconstruction valid even with unbounded cluster sizes. For a fixed known bounded Borel target, retaining positions and angular marks yields the corresponding identification from the complete marked covariance, using signed overlap channels. Restricting the observation to an interior spatial window imposes both angular and logarithmic-spatial constraints. The maximal number of descendants of one germ becomes a rectangle-occupancy number for a subgroup of $\mathbb{R}^2$, finite exactly when that subgroup is discrete. Explicit rank-one laws illustrate what counts forget, while environmental mixtures show why deterministic identification does not extend by averaging covariances.

papers.title: New examples of non-unique enhancements for triangulated categories
papers.abstract: We present a general procedure for constructing triangulated categories, linear over a field, with distinct enhancements. Some of our examples can be equipped with a (non-degenerate) t-structure, thereby showing that the existence of a t-structure does not imply uniqueness of enhancements, whether in the strong or weak sense (depending on the example).

papers.title: Normal complex surface singularities with rational homology disk smoothings
papers.abstract: In this paper we show that if the minimal good resolution graph of a normal surface singularity contains at least two nodes (i.e. vertex with valency at least 3) then the singularity does not admit a smoothing with Milnor fiber having rational homology equal to the rational homology of the 4-disk $D^4$ (called a rational homology disk smoothing). Combining with earlier results, this theorem then provides a complete classification of resolution graphs of normal surface singularities with a rational homology disk smoothing, verifying a conjecture of J. Wahl regarding such singularities. Indeed, together with a recent result of J. Fowler we get the complete list of normal surface singularities which admit rational homology disk smoothings.

papers.title: On properness of moduli stacks of $D^{\times}$-shtukas over ramified legs
papers.abstract: Given a maximal order $\mathcal{D}$ of a central division algebra $D$ over a global function field $F$, we prove an explicit necessary and sufficient condition for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{D}^\times$-shtukas to be proper over a finite field (modulo a suitable central action) in terms of the local invariants of $D$ and bounds. Our result extends E. Lau's criterion (Duke Math. J. 140 (2007)) for properness of the leg morphism (or characteristic morphism) away from the ramification locus of $D$ to allow legs at ramified places. We also establish non-emptiness of Newton and Kottwitz-Rapoport strata for moduli stacks of $\mathcal{B}^\times$-shtukas, where $\mathcal{B}$ is a maximal order of a central simple algebra over $F$.

papers.title: On the crystalline Artin--Mumford invariant
papers.abstract: Let $k$ be an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$ and let $W=W(k)$. We prove that the torsion subgroup of $H^3_{\mathrm{cris}}(X/W)$ is a birational invariant of smooth projective varieties over $k$. The proof combines the action of correspondences on Hodge--Witt cohomology and on the first Nygaard piece of the de Rham--Witt complex.

papers.title: On the Hodge Structures of Global Smoothings of Normal Crossing Varieties
papers.abstract:
We study the Hodge theory of smooth fibers of semistable degenerations of compact complex manifolds with central fibers of K\"ahler type. If every stratum of the central fiber is a $\partial\overline{\partial}$-manifold, we prove that the local invariant cycle property in all degrees implies that the nearby fibers satisfy the $\partial\overline{\partial}$-lemma. In middle degree, the corresponding property alone yields a canonical Hodge decomposition on the nearby fibers and an explicit formula, in terms of the limiting mixed Hodge structure, for the signature of the cup-product pairing on each Hodge component. This gives a partial converse to Clemens' local invariant cycle theorem for K\"ahler degenerations.
  As applications, we study global smoothings of ordinary double points and extend results of Friedman and Li on Clemens manifolds. We also apply our results to the non-K\"ahler Calabi--Yau manifolds constructed by Hashimoto--Sano and Sano. In particular, these manifolds satisfy the $\partial\overline{\partial}$-lemma, even though they are not in Fujiki class $\mathcal{C}$, and in Sano's higher-dimensional examples we explicitly determine the failure of the Hodge--Riemann bilinear relations on the middle cohomology.

papers.title: On the tangent bundle and the divisor theory of a general matroid
papers.abstract: Extending classical algebro-geometric constructions to arbitrary matroids, we construct a $K$-class $T_M\in K(M)$ for every loopless matroid $M$. When $M$ is realizable by a linear subspace $L$, $T_M$ recovers the $K$-class of the tangent bundle of the wonderful compactification $W_L$. We derive two formulas for the total Chern class of $T_M$ (one combinatorial and one geometric) and show that the associated Todd class agrees with the Todd class appearing in the matroid Hirzebruch--Riemann--Roch formula. To develop a positivity theory entirely at the combinatorial level, we introduce the notion of a "fake effective cone", a combinatorial analogue of the classical effective cone, and use it to characterize big and nef divisors in $A(M)$. Finally, we define the $\beta_S$ classes, obtained from Cremona conjugates of the classical $\alpha_S$ classes, and study their properties to provide a rich and computable family of combinatorially nef divisors.

papers.title: On the torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups of smooth quasi-projective varieties of rank up to seven
papers.abstract: Let $X$ be a smooth quasi-projective variety. Assume that the (topological) fundamental group $\pi_1(X, x)$ is torsion-free nilpotent. We show that if the first Betti number $b_1(X) \le 3$, then $\pi_1(X, x)$ is isomorphic to either $\mathbb{Z}^n$ for $n = 1, 2, 3$, a lattice in the Heisenberg group $H_3(\mathbb{R})$ or $\mathbb{R} \times H_3(\mathbb{R})$. Moreover, we prove that $\pi_1(X, x)$ is abelian or $2$-step nilpotent if its rank is less than or equal to seven. More precisely, we determine the real nilpotent Lie groups in which torsion-free nilpotent fundamental groups can be embedded as lattices for ranks up to six and seven, respectively. Our main results are a partial positive answer to a question on nilpotent (quasi-)K\"ahler groups posed by Aguilar and Campana.

papers.title: Optimal windowed test functions for bounding analytic ranks of elliptic curves
papers.abstract: Assuming the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, the explicit formula for the L-function of an elliptic curve E/Q bounds the analytic rank of E in terms of the traces a_p for p < e^(2L), for any admissible test function supported on a window [-L,L]. In rank computations this test function is usually fixed in advance, typically to a Fejer-type kernel; optimising it for an individual L-function goes back to Booker, and an earlier test on quadratic twists of rank about 7 found the gain to be small. We choose, for each individual curve, the test function that minimises the resulting bound within a finite-dimensional space supported on [-L,L], certify the result, and measure the gain systematically, up to the current record curves. The minimiser is the solution of a linear system with the Gram matrix of the Weil quadratic form of E, and the optimal bound equals the reciprocal of the corresponding reproducing kernel at the central point, which we call the radix Riemanniana of E. Because the Fejer-type kernel lies in this space, the optimised bound is never weaker. We certify every bound with ball arithmetic, check the prime-side evaluation against the zero side computed independently from the zeros of L(E,s), and benchmark against the fixed kernel on 1642 curves from Cremona's tables, 2500 curves from the Stein-Watkins database and a set of curves with conductors up to 3*10^16. Depending on the sample and on the stopping criterion, the number of primes required to pin down the analytic rank decreases by 8-23% in aggregate. For individual curves of large conductor the decrease ranges from 0% to 43%. Within each sample the gain is largest at rank 0 and decreases with the rank; it grows again, and by a much larger factor, in the regime of large rank and large conductor where the computation is most expensive. On the smallest-conductor curves of rank 28-31 in the ICARM leaderboard the optimised kernel needs 84-85% fewer primes to certify the rank. For the current record, the rank-32 curve #4239 of Elkies, Klagsbrun and Li, it certifies r_an<=32 under GRH with 2.53*10^9 primes - the first upper bound for this curve - and hence r_an=32 under GRH and BSD, while the fixed kernel, certified at L=12.40 with 2 481 819 193 primes, is still 0.39 above the target. On all 395 leaderboard curves of rank 24-31, with primes below 10^10, the optimised kernel certifies r_an<= r on 379 curves and the fixed kernel on 372; where both succeed the fixed kernel needs a median of 4.0 times as many primes. We validate the fixed-kernel baseline by reproducing every published value of Bober and of Klagsbrun, Sherman and Weigandt with an independent implementation.

papers.title: Pencils of projective hypersurfaces, Griffiths heights and geometric invariant theory. II Hypersurfaces with semihomogeneous singularities
papers.abstract:
This paper establishes a formula for the stable Griffiths height of the middle-dimensional cohomology of a pencil of projective hypersurfaces $H$, with semihomogeneous singularities, over some smooth projective curve $C$. This formula appears as Theorem 5.1 in the first part of this paper (arxiv:2506.15334).
  The proof of this formula relies on the strategy developed in my previous work (arxiv:2212.11019v3) to derive an expression for this Griffiths height when the only singularities of the fibers of $H$ over $C$ are ordinary double points. To deal with general semihomogeneous singularities, we complement this strategy by the construction of a finite covering $C'$ of $C$ such that the pencil $H' = H \times_C C'$ over $C'$ admits a smooth model $\widetilde{H}'$ with semistable fibers with smooth components. This allows us to circumvent the delicate issue of the determination of the elementary exponents attached to the singular fibers of $H/C$.

papers.title: Phases in the cyclic quantum dilogarithm: correction to "Cyclic quantum Teichm\"uller theory"
papers.abstract: We first correct $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-phase issues in the basic definition around the cyclic quantum dilogarithm operators in [Ish26]. In particular, the notion of global coefficients must be extended by incorporating additional lifting data forming a $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-cover, and the pentagon relation generally acquires an extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor. Nevertheless, we prove that every point in a regular locus of the partially compactified cluster Poisson variety lifts to a \emph{strict} extended global coefficient, for which this extra $\boldsymbol{\mu}_N$-factor is trivial. Consequently, the original statements of [Ish26] hold for such lifts and are therefore restored.

papers.title: Plancherel Decompositions and Distinctions for $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n+1}$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})\backslash \mathrm{Gl}_{2n}$
papers.abstract:
Let $F$ be a non-Archimedean local field of characteristic zero. We determine the Plancherel decompositions of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n+1}(F)$ and $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})(F)\backslash\mathrm{GL}_{2n}(F)$, where $P(\mathrm{Sp}_{2n})$ denotes the mirabolic subgroup of $\mathrm{Sp}_{2n}$, and study smooth distinction for both spaces. We carry out the local unfolding procedure of arXiv:1203.0039, Section 9.5, constructing unitary isomorphisms with degenerate Whittaker models by successive Fourier transforms. The isomorphism for the even model is already stated there in Example 9.5.17. The resulting Plancherel formulas are direct integrals of normalized parabolic inductions from the tempered duals of $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_{n+1}(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_n(F)\times\mathrm{GL}_n(F)$, respectively, with product Whittaker-Plancherel measures. In the odd case, the parameter map agrees with the prediction of arXiv:2409.04677.
  Using closed parabolic orbits and local Rankin-Selberg integrals, we prove that all representations induced from these tempered data are distinguished for the corresponding model. We also prove that essentially square-integrable representations are not distinguished for the odd model, and that supercuspidal representations are not distinguished for the even model. For the even model with $n=1,2$, we construct distinguished square-integrable representations outside the Plancherel support. Thus, the smooth tempered distinguished spectrum can be strictly larger than the corresponding $L^2$-spectrum. For $\mathrm{GL}_5(F)$, however, we prove that an irreducible tempered representation is $\mathrm{Sp}_4(F)$-distinguished if and only if it is induced from tempered representations of $\mathrm{GL}_2(F)$ and $\mathrm{GL}_3(F)$.

papers.title: Point Modules of Non-Connected Graded Algebras
papers.abstract: As part of a program to extend the homogeneous coordinate ring techniques of Artin-Tate-Van den Bergh to twisted graded Calabi-Yau (tCY) algebras, we initiate the study of point modules of non-connected graded algebras. We define weak and strong point modules of graded quotients of path algebras and compute their respective moduli stacks. We describe the relation between these point stacks and the classical point schemes in the connected graded setting, and we analyze the point stacks of several 2 and 3-dimensional tCY algebras.

papers.title: Poisson laws and arithmetic clusters for rare multiplicative patterns
papers.abstract: We determine when rare observations of completely multiplicative functions have a Poisson law and when arithmetic relations force clusters. For independent prime values on the circle with uniformly bounded $L^2$ densities, we approximate the field of hits of site-dependent targets of Haar mass $O(N^{-1})$ on deterministic masks in $[2,CN]$. The target retains the true prime-site intensities and uses Haar at composite sites, even when the total prime contribution diverges. The exponent $2$ is sharp in the uniform $L^q$ scale for this target and class of masks. Below this threshold, even correct prime intensities can fail at site resolution while the total count remains asymptotically Poisson. A fixed finite exceptional prime environment, possibly atomic and internally dependent, instead produces a conditional cluster law together with an exact environment-determined configuration. With Haar outside that environment, its integer relation lattice determines the compound-Poisson limit of the corrected prefix count and characterizes simple Poisson convergence. Further applications treat rational observations on sparse moving supports, permanent bounded prime biases, and - using a binary arithmetic relation profile - long Borel patterns in a finite abelian group times a torus. Classical marked Chen-Stein comparison provides a common interface.
