A separate deterministic-sequence interface gives correlation identities, transfer criteria and a resolution obstruction, without proving cancellation for Liouville.

papers.title: Quasi-equivalence of relabeled positroid cluster structures
papers.abstract: We prove the Fraser--Sherman-Bennett conjecture on the quasi-equivalence of positroid cluster structures arising from admissibly relabeled plabic graphs. We construct a tilting module from the boundary necklace and obtain a Frobenius categorification of the relabeled cluster structure. By identifying localized characters of rank-one modules with Pl\"ucker coordinates, we match the stable images of the mutable face modules with the summands of a reachable cluster-tilting object in the stable category. The induced derived equivalence yields a unimodular transformation of relative index lattices intertwining the full extended exchange matrices. These comparisons show that the identity map on the coordinate ring is a quasi-cluster isomorphism between the two cluster structures.

papers.title: Rare events in multiplicative sequences: Poisson laws, clusters, and observation
papers.abstract: A multiplicative identity can persist at every scale while disappearing from a rare-event count. Another identity can survive as a cluster whose points lie far apart. Which distinction matters depends on what is observed. We explain this through one completely calculated model: a uniform germ can trigger two occurrences in disjoint spatial windows. Its two marginal counts become Poisson, but their sum need not do so. A coupling identifies the correct same-grid target and separates the mean number of points from the mean number of active germs. We then isolate the additional work required by multiplicative sources: private prime coordinates, weighted relations between windows, corrections to prime-site intensities, and relations visible at the target scale. A final passage from marked configurations to records explains the roles of ties, recognition and observation clocks. Selected results are stated with their hypotheses; a short concordance leads to their proofs. The elementary calculations are proved here, while the arithmetic and functional limit theorems are taken from the four cited research articles.

papers.title: Records, scale flows, and Gaussian limits from lattice Poisson fields
papers.abstract: How does a rare-event field determine the history of its extremes? Starting from the complete signed run-field comparison in Long runs and rare patterns, we develop records, censoring, occupation and Gaussian limits for the resulting lattice Poisson target. The arithmetic input retains every site, full exact length and actual sign, at growing intensity under a one-factor information-intensity budget. Strict integer records, their signed imbalance and logarithmic leadership time have a joint phase-uniform Brownian limit with explicit covariance, independent of the terminal critical field and its extremal paths. Right censoring gives scalar $M_1$ convergence for the visible maximum and $J_1$ convergence for the first-holder sign. Physical occupation instead has a nondegenerate phase-indexed limit. Canonical interpolation connects threshold thinning and a stationary scale flow without identifying their record rules or their Gaussian constants. The signed spatial theory includes weighted exact levels, fixed-window Ornstein-Uhlenbeck paths, two correlated threshold-compression noises, and rectangle fields with explicit grid centering. Direct partition and quadratic-reconstruction proofs provide alternative routes. For each specified observation, the target calculations identify its limit and the dependencies within the joint constructions.

papers.title: Semialgebraic ${C^m}$ solutions to a univariate system of linear inequalities with Nash forcing
papers.abstract:
Let $(A_{ij}(x))_{1 \leq i \leq N, 1 \leq j \leq M}$ be a matrix of univariate semialgebraic functions. We study the solvability of the system of linear inequalities \begin{equation*}
  \sum_{j=1}^M A_{ij}(x)F_j(x)\leq f_i(x) \ \ \text{ for } i = 1, \ldots, N, \end{equation*} where we assume each forcing $f_i$ is a Nash function. We show that the $C^m$ solvability of the system can be characterized by finitely many linear ordinary differential inequalities in $f$ with semialgebraic coefficients depending only on $(A_{ij})$. When the system is solvable, the solution may be chosen semialgebraic, and the proof gives a constructive procedure in the semialgebraic sense. We also study the semimodule structure of admissible forcings, establishing finite generation and lack thereof in various settings.

papers.title: Seven ordered points and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that the ordered GIT quotient of seven points on $\mathbb P^1$ with equal weights is not isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of any arithmetic complex ball quotient. Together with our companion paper and the known positive examples, this determines the equal weight case for every $n\ge6$: such a realization exists precisely for $n=6,8$. The lattice and the algebraic isomorphism are unrestricted, and torsion and divisorial ramification are allowed. The proof combines arithmetic reductions with identities involving Chern classes of fixed subvarieties and intersection inequalities for nef divisors on the GIT quotient. The final comparison includes all fixed components and requires no bound on the degree of an individual fixed curve.

papers.title: Singularities of orthogonal and symplectic determinantal varieties
papers.abstract: Let either $GL(E)\times SO(F)$ or $GL(E)\times Sp(F)$ act naturally on the space of matrices $E\otimes F$. There are only finitely many orbits, and the orbit closures are orthogonal and symplectic generalizations of determinantal varieties, which can be described similarly using rank conditions. In this paper, we study the singularities of these varieties and describe their defining equations. We prove that in the symplectic case, the orbit closures are normal with good filtrations, and in characteristic $0$ have rational singularities. In the orthogonal case we show that most orbit closures will have similar properties, and determine precisely the exceptions to this.

papers.title: Smooth Limits of Stable Manifolds
papers.abstract: Let X be a compact complex manifold of dimension n, and suppose that X is deformation equivalent to a stable manifold. Then X is projective whenever n <=3. We also construct, for every n >=4, smooth families of compact complex manifolds over the unit disc such that every fiber over the punctured disc is a stable manifold, while the central fiber is a non-Kahler Moishezon manifold.

papers.title: Sparse prime surgery in completely multiplicative sequences: Normality, rare-event realization and optimal repair
papers.abstract: We study how changing prime signs affects fixed-word frequencies, rare-event laws and extremes of completely multiplicative sequences. The cost is $d_\sigma(f,g)=\sum_{f(p)\ne g(p)}p^{-\sigma}$. A known theorem of Frantzikinakis-Lemańczyk-de la Rue preserves normality at finite $d_1$; we give its elementary specialization. Using explicit arithmetic inputs from Long runs, we then establish three families of results. For each fixed $0<\sigma\le1$ and almost every base, reversible surgery realizes every stationary finite-intensity marked point-process law along selected scales, with signs, exact excess lengths and converging actual intensity, at arbitrarily small $d_\sigma$ cost and with a prescribed prefix unchanged. Almost surely over all integer scales, the minimum number of prime changes needed for a run of length $\lceil c\log_2N\rceil$ is asymptotic to $c\alpha_c\log_2N$ for $1<c<3/2$, where $\alpha_c\in(0,1/2)$ satisfies $H_2(\alpha_c)=1-1/c$ and $H_2(u)=-u\log_2u-(1-u)\log_2(1-u)$. At each scale, with probability tending to one, symbolic and private large-prime repair maxima coincide on the same random base for $k_N=o(\log N)$; unrestricted prime repair agrees when $k_N=o(\log\log N)$. This comparison transfers the classical lattice laws of runs with errors to adaptive prime repair. Elementary programming from arbitrary bases and an autonomous finite-range-dependent process construction complement these results.

papers.title: Spectral networks, finite webs, and the $T_3$ cubic differential
papers.abstract: We describe spectral networks for cubic differentials on $\mathbf{P}^1$ with exactly three poles all of order two, following observations of Hollands-Neitzke. To do so, we give a precise definition and establish some basic properties of a class of finite webs (corresponding to BPS states in physics) in the cubic differential setting, including their non-vanishing central charge. Turning to the example, we prove that at rational angles the network is totally degenerate; the number of walls and Stokes regions is explicitly computed and depends on an arithmetic criterion. At all other angles, the spectral network is dense in the surface and contains no finite webs, as expected. Physically, this example corresponds to a fundamental building block for a large class of four-dimensional $\mathcal{N}=2$ QFTs with gauge group $\mathrm{SU}(3)$.

papers.title: Stable Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture for finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras
papers.abstract: We prove that finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras associated with non-degenerate quivers with potentials satisfy the stable Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture. In particular, this implies that the brick Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture (also known as the $\tau$-Brauer--Thrall II$'$ conjecture) holds for finite-dimensional Jacobian algebras.

papers.title: String functions and cyclotomic Hecke algebras
papers.abstract: In this paper we study the Kleshchev multipartitions that label simple modules of certain cyclotomic Hecke algebras with parameters $1$ and $-1$. The $2$-residue statistic divides these multipartitions into blocks. We deduce a bivariate generating function for the blocks using representation theory. We also relate the generating functions of multipartitions in a fixed block to string functions associated by Kac and Peterson to irreducible highest weight modules of a type $A_1^{(1)}$ affine Lie algebra. By considering matrices formed by these generating functions, we reprove some results of Kac--Peterson on string functions using the Macdonald identities of Rosengren--Schlosser. As an application, we obtain new infinite product formulas for these generating functions.

papers.title: The arithmetic of critical values II: critical elliptic curves
papers.abstract: In this second chapter of the $\textit{Arithmetic of critical values}$ series (ACV), we study certain double covers $E_f\to\mathbb{P}^1$ whose branch locus coincides with that of a quartic polynomial $f$. We give a direct proof of the fact, already shown non-constructively in ACV I, that the elliptic curves $E_f$ admit a $3$-isogeny. Our methods are Galois-theoretic, and lead us to a thorough analysis of the Galois closure of $f:\mathbb{P}^1\to\mathbb{P}^1$. We exploit its rich geometry to prove a Selmer companionship theorem for the family $E_f$, allowing us to exhibit elements in certain Tate-Shafarevich groups which are visible in an abelian surface. We also give some dynamical and Diophantine applications of our constructions, as well as new examples of Jacobians isogenous to a power of an elliptic curve.

papers.title: The compact double category $\mathbf{Int}(\mathbf{Poly}_*)$ models control flow and data transformations
papers.abstract: Hasegawa showed that control flow in programming languages---while loops and if-then-else statements---can be modeled using traced cocartesian categories, such as the category Set_* of pointed sets. In this paper we define an operad W of wiring diagrams that provides syntax for categories whose control flow moreover includes data transformations, including deleting, duplicating, permuting, and applying pre-specified functions to variables. In the most basic version, the operad underlies Int(Poly_*), where Int(T) denotes the free compact category on a traced category T, as defined by Joyal, Street, and Verity; to do so, we show that Poly_*, as well as any multivariate version of it, is traced. We show moreover that whenever T is uniform---a condition also defined by Hasegawa and satisfied by Poly_*---the resulting Int-construction extends to a double category IInt(T), which is compact in the sense of Patterson. Finally, we construct an operational structure on the double categories IInt(Poly_*) and IInt(Set_*) by which one can track trajectories as they move through the control flow associated to a wiring diagram, and we prove that the resulting operational semantics is computationally adequate, in the sense of Plotkin, for the denotational semantics in which a filled wiring diagram evaluates to a partial function.

papers.title: The Compactness Theorem for Enriched Logic
papers.abstract: The framework of enriched logic extends positive logic (also known as coherent logic) from sets to structures internal to a symmetric monoidal closed category $\mathcal{V}$. This framework was developed by Rosick\'y and the second-named author. The main novelty of this logic is that the arities of the function and relation symbols are now objects in $\mathcal{V}$. We prove the compactness theorem for this enriched logic. That is, a set of $\mathcal{V}$-enriched sequents has a model (internal to $\mathcal{V}$) if every finite subset has a model. To achieve this, we define ultraproducts of enriched structures and prove enriched versions of {\L}os' theorem. We then develop some model-theoretic applications. We start with an enriched version of the model-theoretic method of diagrams, establishing a correspondence between homomorphisms whose domain is some enriched structure $A$ and models of the set $\operatorname{Diag}(A)$ of all enriched atomic formulas with parameters from $A$ that are true in $A$. Combining this with our compactness theorem, we prove amalgamation results, laying the foundations for enriched syntactic types (in the model-theoretic sense). We finish the paper with a collection of examples of $\mathcal{V}$ that our results apply to. Besides recovering the classical case when $\mathcal{V} = \mathbf{Set}$, these include many presheaf toposes, categories of monoid acts, the category of abelian groups and related additive categories, categories of (small) enriched categories, and the categories of posets and pseudometric spaces.

papers.title: The geometric exceptional set for Fano threefolds
papers.abstract: We study the geometric exceptional set in Manin's conjecture for smooth Fano threefolds. We prove that every adjoint rigid surface with $a$-invariant one on a non-product smooth Fano threefold is normal. This yields a description of the geometric exceptional set in terms of the higher-$a$ locus, anticanonical conics, and del Pezzo fibrations. Zariski density arise only from the latter two contributions. For del Pezzo fibrations, we construct a finite collection of parameter covers which controlling the associated breaking maps. We classify their low-genus components for general smooth Fano threefolds yielding examples with potentially Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets in $22$ of the $105$ deformation families. Extending Batyrev-Tschinkel's example, we construct Fano fourfolds with quartic del Pezzo fibrations and an explicit Fano threefold with two degree-six del Pezzo fibrations, all with Zariski dense geometric exceptional sets. For this threefold, the original form of Manin's conjecture fails on every non-empty open subset for every anticanonical height.

papers.title: The Schubert bialgebra
papers.abstract: We introduce a Schubert bialgebra $\mathcal{A}=\bigoplus_{n\geq 0}\mathbb{Z}[x_1,\ldots,x_n]$, in which polynomials in different numbers of variables multiply to zero and the coproduct splits the variables into two consecutive blocks, and study its graded dual $\mathcal{D}$, whose product is concatenation of weak compositions. The Schubert polynomials $\mathfrak{S}_u^n$ form a basis of $\mathcal{A}$; we give an explicit formula for the dual Schubert basis $\Xi_u^n$ of $\mathcal{D}$ via a transition formula to an elementary symmetric basis, and show that the Schubert structure constants $c_{u,v}^w$ are the coefficients of the coproduct of $\mathcal{D}$ in the dual Schubert basis. The product of $\mathcal{D}$ is then lifted to an associative product $\sqcup$ on the free abelian group $\mathcal{BRC}$ of bounded RC graphs, built from a transition map $\mathcal{Z}$ on RC graphs that realizes the Lascoux-Sch\"utzenberger transition formula and generalizes Little's bumping algorithm. Quotienting $\mathcal{BRC}$ by ideals coming from Demazure crystal equivalence, Nadeau-Tewari forest equivalence, and quasi-Yamanouchi equivalence yields manifestly positive Littlewood-Richardson rules for the dual Schubert, dual key, dual forest, and dual slide bases of $\mathcal{D}$. Read on $\mathcal{A}$, these are branching rules: enumerative formulas for splitting a Schubert, key, forest, or slide polynomial across two blocks of variables, and in the Schubert case they compute the Levi branching coefficients of Ressayre-Richmond for $\mathrm{GL}_p\times\mathrm{GL}_q\hookrightarrow\mathrm{GL}_{p+q}$.

papers.title: Three-Element Lucky Sets of Stirling Permutations
papers.abstract: We characterize the three-element sets of lucky car indices that occur when a Stirling permutation of order $n$ is used as a parking function. A set $\{1,x,y\}$, with $1<x<y<2n$, is admissible precisely when $x$ is odd, or $x$ is even and $y$ is odd with $x<n$, or both are even with $x+y\leq2n$. Explicit Stirling words realize every permitted case. The number of admissible sets is $(n-1)(n-2)+2nh-3h(h+1)/2$, where $h=\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. This answers the three-element characterization and enumeration question in Problem 46 of Colmenarejo et al. The complete classification, parking constructions, and enumeration have been checked in Lean. HAL deposit: hal-05800210v1.

papers.title: Torelli Theorem for moduli stacks of vector bundles on tame Deligne Mumford curves
papers.abstract: We prove a Torelli theorem for full moduli stacks of vector bundles of rank at least three with fixed determinant on a smooth, proper, geometrically connected, tame Deligne--Mumford curve of coarse genus at least two over an arbitrary field $k$. We also prove a Torelli theorem for the full moduli stack of vector bundles of rank at least three of fixed-degree under an explicit compatibility hypothesis. The method is intrinsic to the stack: faithful special-linear linearizations recover Picard stacks, and determinants of tangent complexes recover the canonical principal polarization. This is the first part in a series of two papers.

papers.title: Toric schemes and integral models for Shimura varieties with $\Gamma_1(p)$-type level
papers.abstract: We propose a conjectural theory of $p$-integral models of Shimura varieties with level structure at $p$ given by a class of normal subgroups of parahoric subgroups with abelian quotient group. The role of the theory of local models is played in this context by a certain root stack over the local model for parahoric level. The construction of this root stack is based on the "divisor theorem" (a foundational fact about local models) and on the theory of toric varieties in this context, both of which are of independent interest. We prove our conjecture in the case of Shimura varieties of PEL type when the parahoric is an Iwahori (under some additional conditions).

papers.title: Totally elliptic surface group representations
papers.abstract: A surface group representation into a Lie group is called totally elliptic if every simple closed curve on the surface is mapped to an elliptic element of the target group. In this note, we characterize all totally elliptic surface group representations into $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{C}$ by showing that they are either representations into a compact subgroup or Deroin--Tholozan representations.

papers.title: Trilinear Forms for ${\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$ via conjugacy classes
papers.abstract: It is well known that for a finite group \(G\), the number of elements in ${\rm Irr}(G)$ the set of irreducible representations up to isomorphism is the same as the number of elements in ${\rm Conj}(G)$ the set of conjugacy classes in $G$ although there is no natural bijection between these two sets. For $G={\rm GL}_2(\mathbb{F}_q)$, where $\mathbb{F}_q$ is the finite field with $q$ elements, we give a bijection between ${\rm Irr}(G)$ and ${\rm Conj}(G)$, which behaves well with the tensor product of irreducible representations on one side and the product of conjugacy classes on the other. In particular, we relate the dimension of the trilinear forms with the multiplicity of the identity element in the triple product of the corresponding conjugacy classes.

papers.title: Twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of Wronski maps
papers.abstract:
The Wronski map is a central object of study in osculating Schubert calculus, and has been the focus of much work in real algebraic geometry over the last few decades due to its remarkable reality properties. In this work, we study it over arbitrary fields through the lens of quadratically-enriched enumerative geometry. A basic obstruction is that the Wronski map is not oriented in general, so existing approaches do not apply directly. To that end, we introduce twisted $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees of finite flat lci maps of schemes, which generalize ordinary $\mathbb{A}^1$-degrees by allowing us to twist an orientation by the equation of a divisor, and $\mathbb{A}^1$-chambers, which generalize the notion of connected component of a real manifold.
  We then show that a certain weighted count of the fibers of the Wronski map depends only on the action of the absolute Galois group of the base field on the roots of the Wronski polynomial. This unifies Eremenko and Gabrielov's work on real degrees of Wronski maps, Levinson and Purbhoo's work on the character orientation of the real Wronski map, and Brazelton's work on enriched degrees of Wronski maps into one framework.

papers.title: Typical representations of admissible type I algebraic supergroups
papers.abstract: We study typical representations of an admissible type I algebraic supergroup $G$. We prove that, for a dominant weight $\lambda$, the induced supermodule $H^0_G(\lambda)$ is simple if and only if $\lambda$ is typical and the induced module $H^0_{G_{\mathrm{ev}}}(\lambda)$ for the even subgroup $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$ is simple. We establish equivalences between typical blocks for $G$ and blocks for $G_{\mathrm{ev}}$, and give a projectivity criterion for Kac modules over every Frobenius kernel. For connected $SpO(2\ell|2)$ over an algebraically closed field of odd characteristic, we classify all simple projective supermodules over Frobenius kernels.

papers.title: Values of the Huang–Ma invariant
papers.abstract: We prove the binary-value conjecture of Huang and Ma for integer matrices admitting a fixed positive diagonal skew-symmetrizer. We determine the exact set of values in every size and construct matrices realizing each value.

papers.title: Weak action representability of $2$-nilpotent groups
papers.abstract:
In this article, we investigate the representability of actions of the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ of $2$-nilpotent groups. We first provide an algebraic characterisation of derived actions in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ in terms of the group $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ of central automorphisms of an object $X$. We also characterise the morphisms $B \to \operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ that define an action of $B$ on $X$ in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$.
  We then show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not action representable, and that the existence of a weak representation is related to the amalgamation property. We prove that the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is weakly action representable, by exhibiting a strong amalgam of a suitable family of abelian subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$: an explicit weak representing object of $X$ is the abelian group $\operatorname{Hom}(X/[X,X],\operatorname{Z}(X))$.
  Finally, we show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not locally algebraically cartesian closed.

papers.title: Weighted configurations and the nonexistence of arithmetic ball quotient compactifications
papers.abstract: We prove that, for every $n\ge9$, no ordered GIT quotient of $n$ points on $\mathbb P^1$ with positive rational weights smaller than one and of total weight two is isomorphic to the Baily--Borel compactification of an arithmetic complex ball quotient. The weights may lie on stability walls, and the lattice may have torsion and ramify along divisors. No compatibility with a prescribed period map is assumed. The proof compares homomorphisms from the tangent bundle to line bundles of negative degree with normal bundles of arithmetic fixed subvarieties. We describe these homomorphisms through coincident marked points and prove vanishing statements for their kernels. The comparison, together with integrality of Chern classes and the invariant theory of finite reflection groups, gives the nonexistence theorem without a Fano assumption on the GIT quotient.

papers.title: Whittaker Functionals for Exceptional Representations
papers.abstract: In the study of automorphic forms on covering groups, Kazhdan-Patterson gives a formula that determines when the Whittaker functionals of induced representations can be descended to exceptional representations. In this paper, first, following the original approach given by Kazhdan-Patterson and applying the block-compatible 2-cocycle of Banks-Levy-Sepanski, we fill in several details omitted in the original proof. Secondly, we compare the formula of Kazhdan-Patterson with that of McNamara and Gao, which is formulated in a more general setting.
